Subject: Clarify data-role ownership & export safeguards — DPA/Order Form

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re aligning the MSA + Order Form redlines with your security team and want to lock two things down before next Friday’s exec review:

1) Role delegation for processors/sub-processors (which fields in the Order Form map to 'Processor' vs 'Controller' activities).
2) Practical export safeguard expectations for multi-region failover (what ClearPath needs vs our standard SCCs + transfer impact addendum).

I attached a quick 'DPA Safeguard Matrix' that maps clause ownership and suggested language for the Order Form exhibits — can you confirm whether the matrix reflects your expectations (especially rows 4–6 about temporary in-region caching and analytics KV storage)?

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute tech + legal sync on Thursday. Proposed times: 10:00 or 15:30 CEST.

Thanks,
Sean

Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify data-role ownership & export safeguards — DPA/Order Form

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the matrix, that’s very helpful. Quick answers:
- Rows 1–3 look correct (we will be Controller for patient identifiers; Redwood will be Processor for model inference and embeddings).
- Rows 4–6: temporary in-region cache is acceptable for latency, but we require documented retention limits and the ability to disable cross-border caching per-tenant.
- For analytics/KV: we need to confirm that telemetry in aggregate will not contain PHI and request explicit carve-outs in the Order Form exhibit.

Procurement has requested a consolidated redline for the Order Form (they can only accept DocuSign-ready attachments). I’ll loop in external counsel if we need additional legal language on SCCs.

We can do Thu 15:30 CEST.

—Marta
Marta Alvarez
Head of Security & Compliance, ClearPath Health

Hi all —

I reviewed the redline and the safeguard matrix. A few legal notes for SCCs + transfer-impact:
- The 'per-tenant cache disable' should be a contractual right for the Controller. Wording: "Customer may instruct Processor to disable cross-border caching for Customer Data; Processor will implement within the timeframe set out in Exhibit B."
- Add a 30-day audit window where Customer can request evidence that analytics telemetry was de-identified per the definition — reasonable scope (sampling + descriptions).
- For fallback regions: include clear routing priority and a committed notification cadence if we need to route outside EU for short-term failover.

I can propose specific SCC clauses if you want; I recommend we provide two alternatives (Redwood standard SCCs + an enhanced SCCs pack for healthcare customers).

Regards,
Jurek Novak
Partner, Novak Law (external counsel)
